Concerns.Title: The Clan at the Poles
Concerns.Pitch: There is water, and there is shade; sit, and let the hard part wait until you have drunk. My guest is a salt-carrier. She took my cloth four days ago with my own clan behind her, and they are behind her still: they are sitting at the poles. She broke a carriage-contract with them and walked off the pans with the salt. I have not asked her business. They told me anyway. They keep the oath to the hour, as they should; at dawn her third day is over, and they will take her. And then I stand between my guest and my own blood, which is what I swore here, under these poles, and what I would rather not find out I meant. Hear me plainly: I am not asking you to fight my clan. They are people, and the oath binds you as it binds them. There are other ways out of the morning.
Concerns.Thanks: Dawn came. My clan stood up from the poles and went home without their salt or their carrier, and nobody's cloth was torn. I did not have to learn what I meant. I owe you that, and I will not put a price on it.

Approaches.Label: If you are sworn, take her under your own cloth when mine ends.
Approaches.Objective: Name the salt-carrier your guest before her third day ends

Approaches.Label: Pay my clan what the contract was worth.
Approaches.Objective: Pay the clan the carriage-contract's worth
Approaches.OfferText: Pay the clan 120 drams for the salt.

Approaches.Label: Read the cord of the first oath, and say what it says to the clan.
Approaches.Objective: Read the knotted cord of the first oath at the First Tent

Refusal.Text: I won't stand in a clan's quarrel. No.
Refusal.Reply: Refused, and said aloud, under the poles. That is all the cloth asks of you. Drink before you go.
